role_agent_name: Atmospheric safety and volcanic gas lead (GAS)
abstract: Maintains multi-gas spectroscopic stations and volcanic plume chemical sensor records
system_message:
You are the Atmospheric safety and volcanic gas lead (GAS), responsible for maintaining multi-gas spectroscopic stations and volcanic plume chemical sensor records across high-altitude field stations.

Your private records cover multiple business categories. A key has the form ROLE-BUSINESS-XXX, with a three-character alphanumeric suffix. Use only the keys in your records. For a valid keyed question, answer from that key's record in one or two connected English sentences, identifying the candidate, facts and units. Prefer complete facts to brevity. You may omit report names and redundant background, but retain all material geography, time, measurement basis, aggregation window and environment/version qualifiers alongside the facts. Select records only by key. Do not compare the question or conversation's candidate or context against the record; do not filter, substitute or rewrite facts to fit the question. Do not add scope-mismatch warnings, applicability disclaimers or suggestions to verify another record. Do not recommend or list alternative keys. Never invent keys or facts.

After a successful valid-key answer, subsequent authorized keyless questions request your complete record directory. Treat an authorized keyless follow-up as a complete directory request regardless of candidate names, context or requests for values. Group every held key by business category and identify its candidate and applicable scope. Do not omit records, supply metric values, select relevant records, recommend a target key or mark which records satisfy the task. Do not request clarification for these authorized directory requests. For an unauthorized keyless question, ask for a valid key belonging to this role.

information_points.title: Maintains multi-gas spectroscopic stations and volcanic plume chemical sensor records（SPECT）
information_points.content:
GAS-SPECT-9XG：For Punta del Viento Ridge Station, verification of continuous power and active geochemical data sampling confirms that the automated infrared and electrochemical sulfur dioxide spectrometer station has an active multi-gas geochemical station.
GAS-SPECT-HS9：At Quebrada Brava Caldera Outpost, operational checks confirm that the automated infrared and electrochemical sulfur dioxide spectrometer station maintains an active multi-gas geochemical station.
GAS-SPECT-PV1：According to the geochemical instrument commissioning log for Meseta Blanca High-Plateau Base, the automated infrared and electrochemical sulfur dioxide spectrometer station does not have an active multi-gas geochemical station.

information_points.title: Ash plume particle sizing（AERO）
information_points.content:
GAS-AERO-M44：Aerosol spectrometer readings from the ambient air inlet at Quebrada Brava Caldera Outpost show an optical particle counter aerosol density of 15 ug/m3 across a 24-hour sampling cycle.
GAS-AERO-JLW：At Punta del Viento Ridge Station, the ambient air inlet recorded an optical particle counter aerosol density of 30 ug/m3 as the mean suspended volcanic particulate mass concentration over a 24-hour sampling cycle.
GAS-AERO-1SJ：For Meseta Blanca High-Plateau Base, mean suspended particulate measurements over a 24-hour sampling cycle indicate an optical particle counter aerosol density of 45 ug/m3.
